newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian bank bond four times oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian bank bond four times oversubscribed.

text.p: A 90 million pound bond offer by the Egyptian state's Arab Land Bank was more than four times oversubscribed, the bank chairman said on Tuesday.

Subscribers applied for bonds worth 493.558 million pounds, or 548 percent of the amount on offer, between the opening on August 31 and the close on September 9, chairman Alaa Ahmed el-Oussyea told Reuters.
Under Egypt's capital market regulations, such issues must stay open for at least 10 days.
The seven-year floating-rate bonds pay interest each six months at 1.5 percentage points below the Central Bank's discount rate, which has stood at 13.5 percent for the past 10 months.
The Arab Land Bank bond has been one of the most attractive on the Egyptian market in recent months, a banker said.

Later this month the Egyptian treasury is offering seven-year bonds with a fixed yield of 11 percent and American Express Bank is offering five-year floating-rate notes linked to three-month treasury bills, which now yield 10.25 percent.
